q.t: Which of these is a factor of 12?
q.e: 12 counters make 3 rows of 4, so 4 divides 12 exactly.

q.t: Which of these is a multiple of 3?
Is 13 a prime number?
o: Yes — the only array is 1 row of 13
q.e: 13 counters cannot be put into equal rows except one long line.

q.t: A rabbit jumps 4 at a time, starting from 0. Which number does it land on?
q.e: After 5 jumps it is at 4 × 5 = 20. It lands only on multiples of 4.

q.t: A frog jumps 3 at a time and a rabbit 4 at a time, both from 0. Where do they FIRST land together?
q.k: min(set(range(3,100,3))&set(range(4,100,4)))
q.e: Frog: 3, 6, 9, 12. Rabbit: 4, 8, 12. 12 is the first number on both lists.

q.t: A number divisible by 5 ends in:
q.e: Every ten is a multiple of 5, so only the ones digit matters: 0 or 5.

q.t: A number divisible by 10 ends in:
q.e: Multiples of 10 are whole tens, with nothing in the ones place.

q.t: Which number is divisible by 2?
q.e: It ends in 8, an even digit.

q.t: Which number is a factor of EVERY number?
q.e: 1 × N = N for every number N.

q.t: How many factors does 10 have?
q.k: len([d for d in range(1,11) if 10%d==0])
q.e: 1, 2, 5, 10 — from the arrays 1 × 10 and 2 × 5.

q.t: How many factors does 20 have?
q.k: len([d for d in range(1,21) if 20%d==0])

q.t: What is the first common multiple of 4 and 6?
q.k: min(set(range(4,100,4))&set(range(6,100,6)))
q.e: 4, 8, 12 and 6, 12 — they meet at 12, not at 4 × 6 = 24.

q.t: What is the first common multiple of 3 and 6?
q.k: min(set(range(3,100,3))&set(range(6,100,6)))
q.e: 6 is itself a multiple of 3, so every 6-jump landing is also a 3-jump landing.

q.t: What is the BIGGEST common factor of 12 and 16?
q.k: max(d for d in range(1,13) if 12%d==0 and 16%d==0)
q.e: Common factors are 1, 2 and 4.

q.t: Which number is prime?
Jumps of 6 and jumps of 8 start at 0. Where do they FIRST meet?
q.k: min(set(range(6,200,6))&set(range(8,200,8)))
q.e: 6, 12, 18, 24 and 8, 16, 24 — they meet at 24, not 48.

q.t: How many factors does 25 have?
q.k: len([d for d in range(1,26) if 25%d==0])
q.e: 1, 5, 25 — the arrays are 1 × 25 and 5 × 5.

q.t: Which number is a multiple of BOTH 2 and 5?
q.e: It ends in 0, so it is a multiple of 10 — and 10 = 2 × 5.

q.t: What common factor of 9 and 21 is bigger than 1?
q.k: max(d for d in range(1,10) if 9%d==0 and 21%d==0)

q.t: What is the only common factor of 14 and 15?
q.e: They are consecutive — a jump bigger than 1 can’t land on two numbers just 1 apart.

q.t: How many factors does 54 have?
q.k: len([d for d in range(1,55) if 54%d==0])
q.e: Pairs: 1 × 54, 2 × 27, 3 × 18, 6 × 9 — that is 8 factors.

q.t: How many common factors do 24 and 36 have?
q.k: len([d for d in range(1,25) if 24%d==0 and 36%d==0])
q.e: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12 divide both.

q.t: What is the first common multiple of 9 and 12?
q.k: min(set(range(9,200,9))&set(range(12,200,12)))

q.t: What is the first common multiple of 5 and 8?
q.k: min(set(range(5,200,5))&set(range(8,200,8)))
q.e: 5 and 8 share no factor except 1, so they first meet at 5 × 8 = 40.

q.t: Mowgli wants to reach Baloo at 30 but NOT land on Sher Khan at 25. Which jump size works?
q.e: 6 is a factor of 30 but not of 25. Jumps of 1 or 5 would land on 25.

q.t: What jump size bigger than 1 lands on both 21 and 35?
q.k: max(d for d in range(2,22) if 21%d==0 and 35%d==0)
q.e: 21 = 3 × 7 and 35 = 5 × 7, so 7 is a common factor.

q.t: Which number is divisible by 10 but NOT by 2?
q.e: 10 = 2 × 5, so every multiple of 10 is also a multiple of 2.

q.t: ‘Factors of an even number must be even.’ Is this true?
q.e: One counter-example is enough to show it is false.

q.t: A spider jumps 3 and a grasshopper jumps 6, both from 0. Their common landings are the multiples of:
q.e: Every 6-jump landing is also a spider landing, because the spider just takes two hops of 3.

q.t: How many multiples of 4 are there from 1 to 50?
A frog jumps 3 and a rabbit jumps 5, both from 0. On how many numbers from 1 to 100 do BOTH land?
q.k: len(set(range(3,101,3))&set(range(5,101,5)))
q.e: They meet at multiples of 15: 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90.

q.t: A kangaroo jumps 6 and a rabbit jumps 8, both from 0. Where do they meet for the SECOND time?
q.k: sorted(set(range(6,200,6))&set(range(8,200,8)))[1]
q.e: They first meet at 24, and then every 24 after that: 48.

q.t: What is the BIGGEST jump size that lands on both 24 and 36?
q.k: max(d for d in range(1,25) if 24%d==0 and 36%d==0)
q.e: Common factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 — the biggest is 12.

q.t: What is the smallest number that is a multiple of 2, 3 and 5?
q.k: min(n for n in range(1,100) if n%2==0 and n%3==0 and n%5==0)
q.e: It must end in 0 (for 2 and 5) and be a multiple of 3: 10 and 20 fail, 30 works.

q.t: Can an ODD number have an EVEN factor?
o: Never — an even number times anything is even
q.e: If an even number were a factor, the odd number would be even × something, which is even.

q.t: Which number between 40 and 50 is a multiple of both 3 and 4?
q.k: min(n for n in range(41,50) if n%3==0 and n%4==0)
q.e: Common multiples of 3 and 4 are 12, 24, 36, 48 …

q.t: 36 laddoos are packed into boxes, the same number in each box. There must be more than 1 box and more than 1 laddoo per box. How many ways can this be done?
q.k: len([d for d in range(2,36) if 36%d==0])
q.e: Factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Leave out 1 and 36: 7 ways.

q.t: Which number has EXACTLY 3 factors?
q.e: 49 has 1, 7, 49. 15 and 21 have 4 factors; 12 has 6.

q.t: Two bells ring together at 9:00. One rings every 6 minutes, the other every 10 minutes. After how many minutes do they next ring together?
q.k: min(set(range(6,200,6))&set(range(10,200,10)))
q.e: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 10, 20, 30 — the first common multiple is 30.

q.t: Which number is divisible by 2, by 5 AND by 10?
q.e: Only a number ending in 0 is divisible by all three.
